data.title: Edge cases and error behaviour
body: # Edge cases and error behaviour
- **Origin:** every case derived from a diamond in [the flows](DOC-22), an invariant in [the states](DOC-20), or from a real observation
## Principles
1. **Never blame the user.** "No active sprint found" — not "you did not create a sprint".
2. **Message = what happened + why + what to do.** The third part is mandatory, and it must contain a command that can be copied.
3. **Corrupted data does not stop the work.** One broken file must not hide the rest of the journal.
4. **Never "something went wrong".** If we do not know the cause, we say which file exactly and which operation.
5. **Errors under `--json` are JSON too.** Otherwise the agent gets a spoiled stream.
## A. Environment
| Situation | Behaviour | Message |
| Not a git repository | Exit 1, we create nothing | `kadence lives inside a git repository, and there is none here.` + `git init` |
| A command before `init` | Exit 1 | `.kadence/ not found. Run: npx kadence init` |
| `user.email` not configured | Exit 1 | `Git does not know who you are — there is nobody to write the event from.` + `git config user.email you@example.com` |
| **The `events/2026-09/` directory has vanished** | **`mkdir -p` before every write, silently** | none — this is a normal state |
| `.kadence/` exists but is empty | Treat as initialised, the journal is empty | `No tasks yet. Create the first one: kadence task add "..."` |
| No write permission | Exit 1 | `Cannot write to .kadence/events/ — no permission.` + the path |
| A repeated `init` | We destroy nothing, exit 0 | `kadence is already initialised.` |

**About the vanished directory.** Git does not version empty directories, so `events/2026-09/` disappears when switching to a branch that had no events that month. During the spike this reproduced **twice**. So `mkdir -p` on every write is not an optimisation but a requirement, and it cannot be "removed as redundant".
## B. Corrupted data
| Situation | Behaviour | Message |
| Broken JSON in one event | Skip it, read the rest, fold | `Skipped 1 corrupted event: events/2026-09/01J8….json` (stderr) |
| A truncated file (an interrupted write) | The same | the same |
| An event of an unknown type | Skip it, **not an error** | `Skipped 2 events of a newer format. Update kadence.` |
| `state.json` corrupted | Delete it silently and rebuild | none |
| `state.json` deleted by hand | Rebuild | none — **invariant I6** |
| More than 20% of the journal corrupted | Exit 1 | `The journal is seriously corrupted: 34 of 120 events are unreadable.` + `git status`, `git checkout .kadence/` |

**Why skipping rather than crashing.** The journal merges automatically and may contain events from future versions of kadence. Crashing on an unknown type would make upgrading in a team impossible: the first person to upgrade breaks the CLI for everyone else.
The 20% threshold separates "one event got spoiled" from "something is systematically wrong" — in the second case staying silent is dangerous.
## C. Git operations
| Situation | What happens | Behaviour |
| `git rebase` | Commits rewritten, **the event files are the same** | Works. ULIDs are unchanged, order by ULID is preserved |
| **`rebase` with a `drop` of a commit** | **The event disappears from history** | **Data loss.** The state is recomputed without it — silently and correctly from the journal's point of view |
| `squash merge` | All the branch's events in one commit | Works with no difference |
| `cherry-pick` of an event | The event appears in two branches with the same ULID | Deduplication by ULID while folding |
| `git revert` of a commit with an event | The event file is removed by a new commit | The state is recomputed without it. **This is the only legal way to "undo" an event** |
| Detached HEAD | Reading works, writing too | Warning: `You are not on a branch — the event may be lost when you switch` |
| **`git worktree`** | Each working tree has its own `.kadence/` | The path is resolved from the root of the **current** tree, not from the main repository |
| Shallow clone (`--depth`) | The journal is complete, because it is files, not history | Works |
| `.kadence/` in `.gitignore` entirely | The journal is not committed | Warning on `init`: `.kadence/ is in .gitignore — the point of kadence is lost` |

**About `rebase --drop` we have to be honest:** we cannot detect it. The event simply disappears, and the journal stays internally consistent. That is an acceptable price for living inside git — but it belongs in the documentation, not in something the user works out alone.

**About worktree.** Backlog.md has an open issue #558 about exactly this: their MCP server wrote to the main repository instead of the worktree. The mistake is natural and expensive, so we fix the rule in advance.
## D. Concurrency and time
| Situation | Behaviour |
| Two processes writing at once (a human + an agent) | No conflict: different ULIDs → different files. The write is atomic via temp + `rename` |
| Two processes rebuilding `state.json` | Atomic write; the loser overwrites — the content is identical |
| **The clock went backwards** | The ULID is generated **monotonically within the process**: if the new time is ≤ the previous one, the random part is incremented |
| The clocks on different machines diverged | It does not matter: order comes from the ULID, not from `ts` — **invariant I2** |
| Two machines created an event in the same millisecond | 80 bits of randomness; across 50,000 ULIDs there were no collisions ([measured](DOC-6)) |
## E. Domain boundaries
| Situation | Behaviour | Message |
| `task move` of a task that does not exist | Exit 1 | `There is no task KAD-99.` + `kadence task list` |
| A transition into the same state | The event is **not written**, exit 0 | `KAD-42 is already in_progress.` |
| An invalid transition (`backlog` → `done`) | **We write the event, we allow it** | `The task went from backlog straight to done, skipping in_progress.` |
| A task into a closed sprint | Reject, keep the event | `Sprint 4 was closed on 2026-08-30 — its velocity is not rewritten.` |
| `sprint close` with no active sprint | Exit 1 | `There is no active sprint.` + `kadence sprint create "..."` |
| Tasks without an estimate at close | Close, warn | `3 tasks without an estimate did not enter velocity.` + the list |
| An empty sprint | Close, velocity = 0 | `Sprint closed. No task was completed.` |
| A very long title (>200 characters) | Truncate in the list, full in `show` | none |
| A title with a line break | Accept, escape on output | none |

**Why an invalid transition is allowed.** Forbidding it would force a person to take two steps for the sake of a formality, and the journal would record the real intent anyway. We warn, but we do not block: kadence describes the work, it does not govern it.
## F. Agent mode
| Situation | Behaviour |
| An error under `--json` | JSON on stdout: `{"schema":"kadence/v1","ok":false,"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"..."}}`, the exit code unchanged |
| A warning under `--json` | stderr only — stdout stays pure JSON |
| The agent did not set `KADENCE_SOURCE` | `source: "human"` by default. **We do not guess** |
| The agent writes hundreds of events in a row | There is no limit, but `state.json` is rebuilt once at the end |
| An unknown flag | Exit 2 + a hint at the nearest command |
## G. Scale
| Situation | Behaviour |
| 10,000+ events | `state.json` is mandatory: 6 ms against 140 ms ([measured](DOC-8)) |
| The working copy has bloated | Compaction into `events/archive/` — otherwise 39 MB at 10k events |
| A task description a megabyte long | Accept it; descriptions are separate files, they do not enter the journal |
## What the tests cover
Sections B, C and D belong in full to the "resilience" set in [SPEC.md](../../SPEC.md). The three most important:
1. Deleting `state.json` does not change the state (I6)
2. A vanished `events/` directory is recreated on write
3. A corrupted event does not hide the rest of the journal
